elements.element: Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer against third-party IP infringement claims relating to services/deliverables
elements.evidence: "IBM will indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Customer ... against that claim" for claims that "Materials or Base Components ... infringe that party's patent, trademark, copyright, or trade secret" (note: the official check reports this head as not present)
"the Customer, its Enterprise and their respective employees, officers, agents and directors"

elements.element: Indemnity for claims arising from Vendor's breach of law
elements.evidence: Indemnity is limited to infringement: "This is IBM's entire obligation to Customer with regard to any claim of infringement." No breach-of-law head anywhere; the redline adds none.

elements.element: Indemnity for data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: No data-breach indemnity head; only patent/trademark/copyright/trade secret claims are covered.

elements.element: Indemnity for Vendor gross negligence / wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: Gross negligence/wilful misconduct appears only as a carve-out from Customer's indemnity: "Customer shall be relieved of its indemnification duty ... to the extent that IBM's bad faith, willful misconduct or gross negligence" — no Vendor indemnity for it.

elements.element: Standard procedure: prompt notice to Vendor
elements.evidence: Only sub-paragraph "b." is reproduced; the notice condition (presumably "a.") is not in the supplied text.

elements.element: Standard procedure: Vendor control of defence and settlement
elements.evidence: "allows IBM to control ... the defense and any related settlement negotiations"
"cooperates with IBM in, the defense and any related settlement negotiations"

elements.element: Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content
elements.evidence: "arises out of the Content, the Customer Components"

elements.element: Customer's indemnity limited to Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: "or Customer's breach of applicable law; or"
"IBM will indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Customer ... infringe that party's patent, trademark, copyright, or trade secret"
"IBM is not responsible for third party claims based on:" — the enumerated exclusions other than item 3 are not reproduced.

elements.element: Remedies: procure continued use, modify, replace
elements.evidence: "to enable Customer to continue to use ... or to modify them, or replace them with non-infringing Materials or Base Components"
"IBM will give Customer a credit equal to the amount Customer paid IBM ... up to a maximum of twelve (12) months of applicable charges"

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No super-cap language; the only monetary limit is the refund credit "up to a maximum of twelve (12) months of applicable charges".

offending_extra_words: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and arises out of the Content, the Customer Components or Customer's breach of applicable law; or
reasons: The redline only narrows the Customer-side indemnity carve-out; it does not add the preferred Vendor indemnity heads for Vendor's breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, so the locked preferred level remains incomplete.
Fallback is also incomplete: there is no 3× annual fees super-cap on the Vendor indemnity (the clause instead caps recovery at a 12-month credit and declares the infringement remedy exclusive).

Minimality fails the official gate (changed-character ratio 0.629 > 0.600): the operation rewrites nearly the whole of item 3 rather than replacing the offending phrase "is related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" with a short substitute, and it introduces "the Customer Components" beyond the playbook's 'customer-provided content and customer breach of law'.

Intent is preserved — the surrounding indemnity mechanics, exclusions and remedies remain effective and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is created (Content/Customer Components are agreement-defined constructs used elsewhere).
